title: Diatomacearum Species Typicae
citation: Theodor Eulenstein, Diatomacearum Species Typicae, Century I, ed. 1, nos. 1–100 (Stuttgart, 1867); Century I, ed. 2, nos. 1–100 (Dresden, 1869); Century II, nos. 101–[200?] (Dresden, c.1869).
tags: Eulenstein; diatoms; slide series; numbered sets; Stuttgart; Dresden; provenance
note: A numbered commercial/subscription series of mounted diatom species. Harvard's Farlow index is reconstructed from surviving microscope-slide labels and the printed schedule of taxa inside the box cover, and records surviving copies across multiple collections. The series therefore joins object, number, taxon and publication apparatus directly.
links: Harvard University Herbaria & Libraries: https://www.huh.harvard.edu/eulenstein-diatomacearum-species-typicae; Harvard bibliography: https://www.huh.harvard.edu/published-collections-bibliography-and-locations

authors: Per Theodor Cleve and Johann Diedrich Möller
title: Diatoms
citation: Per Theodor Cleve and Johann Diedrich Möller, Diatoms, Parts I–VI, nos. 1–324 (Upsala: Edquist / Esaias Edquists Boktryckeri, 1877–1882), with serially published schedules of localities and taxa and accompanying microscope slides.
tags: Cleve; J.D. Möller; diatoms; slide series; numbered sets; Sweden; provenance
note: A six-part object-text series comprising 324 numbered strewn mounts on microscope slides. Harvard explicitly links the slide labels to the serially published schedules and records surviving copies in multiple institutional collections, making it unusually strong evidence for nineteenth-century serial distribution of prepared slides.
links: Harvard University Herbaria & Libraries: https://www.huh.harvard.edu/cleve-m%C3%B6ller-diatoms; Harvard bibliography: https://www.huh.harvard.edu/published-collections-bibliography-and-locations

title: Fred Enock 1845-1916 — The Man and His Work
citation: Brian M. Davidson, “Fred Enock 1845–1916 — The Man and His Work,” Microscopy 36 (Autumn 1992): 657–674.
tags: Fred Enock; slide maker; insect slides; mounting; trade; surviving slides
note: Maker-specific study of Fred Enock, whose reputation rested heavily on exceptionally prepared and mounted microscope slides. Later provenance records and sale catalogues cite this article when documenting surviving Enock material.

title: J.T. Norman - Microscopical Mounter
citation: Brian Bracegirdle, “J.T. Norman - Microscopical Mounter,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 37, pt. 7 (1996): 514–535.
tags: J.T. Norman; mounter; slide maker; trade; labels; family workshop
note: Dedicated study of J.T. Norman as a microscopical mounter, including surviving mounts and documentary evidence for the Norman family slide-making enterprise. It is a core bridge between named maker, workshop records and identifiable slides.
links: Museum of the History of Science, Oxford: https://www.mhs.ox.ac.uk/collections/library/catalogue-simple/classifications/index6fb5.html?id=31; Norman research page: https://microscopist.net/NormanJT.html

title: The Norman inheritance: renovating
language: Brian Darnton, “The Norman inheritance: renovating, conserving, mounting and evaluating the material,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 38 (1999): 377–383.
verification: Norman; surviving slides; conservation; remounting; evaluation; provenance
links: Object-led treatment of inherited Norman material centred on renovation, conservation, mounting and evaluation. The physical preparations themselves are the subject of the article, making it especially useful for the afterlife of commercial slide collections.

title: Mikroskopische Präparate: Hersteller und Lieferanten: eine Zusammenstellung aus zwei Jahrhunderten
citation: Karlheinz A. Rosenbauer, Mikroskopische Präparate: Hersteller und Lieferanten: eine Zusammenstellung aus zwei Jahrhunderten, Bd. 1 (Darmstadt: GIT-Verlag, 2003).
tags: slide makers; suppliers; Germany; Netherlands; Belgium; Austria; Switzerland; Spain; Czechoslovakia; Denmark

Volume 1 covers several continental European markets and includes bibliography and index; library subject headings explicitly identify microscope slides and specimen mounting as its historical subjects.

title: John Thomas Norman junior: his career
language: Peter B. Paisley, “John Thomas Norman junior: his career, his mounts, his times and his family,” Micscape Magazine (July 2012).
verification: John Norman junior; surviving slides; handwriting; labels; Watson; Challenger; attribution
links: A slide-by-slide attribution study using handwriting, labels, construction, provenance and retail stickers to distinguish John Norman junior's output. It also identifies surviving mounts linking Norman production to Watson retailing and Challenger material, while marking speculative claims as such.

title: Edmund Wheeler: a man of parts
citation: Brian Stevenson and Stanley Warren, “Edmund Wheeler: a man of parts,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 42 (Summer 2015): 339–354.
tags: Edmund Wheeler; slide maker; dealer; trade; retail; Topping; Möller
note: Maker-and-dealer study of Edmund Wheeler, a major commercial preparer and retailer. The article is directly relevant to slides as traded objects because Wheeler's business both produced preparations and retailed stock from other makers, including material associated with Topping and J.D. Möller.

title: An early slide collection: exploring a connection to Quekett
citation: Howard Lynk, “An early slide collection: exploring a connection to Quekett,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 42 (Winter 2015): 491–510.
tags: John Thomas Quekett; early slides; provenance; handwriting; attribution; surviving collection
note: Detailed object-provenance study of a 138-slide collection. Eleven slides bear the signature 'J. Quekett' and ten are dated August 1843; the article uses labels, handwriting, material features and provenance limits to test rather than simply assert attribution.
